relevant_findings.topic: Painting contractor scope for foundation in NC
relevant_findings.finding: Foundation coating in new construction is a PAINTING scope, not a waterproofing scope. The painting contractor's work is the above-grade cosmetic coating — the visible foundation band (typically 12-36 inches above grade) that receives a decorative/protective coating matching the house color scheme. Below-grade waterproofing (40-60 mils DFT, sheet membrane, bituminous systems) is a specialty trade and is explicitly excluded from this spec. This is typically a small add-on line item, not a standalone project.

relevant_findings.topic: Foundation substrate types — poured concrete and CMU
relevant_findings.finding: Two foundation substrate types are in scope: poured concrete and CMU block. Both are cementitious substrates classified under SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY. Poured concrete foundations are smooth with potential form-release agents, laitance, and bug holes. CMU foundations have open-cell voids requiring block filler before coating. Both substrates are alkaline (pH 12-14 when new) and require alkali-resistant primer.

relevant_findings.topic: Surface preparation — CSP must match coating thickness
relevant_findings.finding: Concrete Surface Profile (CSP) must match the intended coating thickness. CSP 1-2 (smooth to light) for thin cosmetic coatings (<10 mils). CSP 3-5 (medium to heavy) for thick waterproofing systems (40-60 mils). For the above-grade cosmetic coating in this spec, CSP 1-2 is appropriate. 83% of foundation coating failures originate from insufficient surface roughness per doctrine.

Poured concrete foundations retain form-release agents (bond-breakers) and laitance (weak cement paste layer) from the casting process. These MUST be removed before coating. Form-release agents are waxy/oily substances that prevent coating adhesion. Laitance is a soft, powdery layer of cement fines and water that forms on the surface during curing. Removal methods: mechanical abrasion (wire brush, grinder), abrasive blasting, or chemical detergents.

Efflorescence (white salt deposits) must be removed before coating. Coating over active efflorescence causes osmotic blistering — salts continue to migrate through the coating, creating pressure bubbles that lift the film. Treatment: dry brush removal for light deposits, TSP wash for moderate, phosphoric acid for severe. Moisture source must be identified — efflorescence indicates moisture migration through the foundation wall.

Foundation wall moisture content must be at or below 4% at the coating surface before application. This is a HARD STOP — do not coat if MC exceeds 4%. Note: this is stricter than the masonry wall spec (12% MC) because foundation walls are in direct ground contact with continuous moisture exposure. Testing with electronic moisture meter at multiple points across the above-grade band.

relevant_findings.topic: Grade-line transition — NEVER caulk the gap
relevant_findings.finding: The grade-line transition where siding meets foundation requires a 3/8-inch gap with Z-flashing for drainage. This gap must NEVER be caulked. Caulking the gap seals the drainage plane, trapping moisture behind the siding and causing catastrophic rot, mold, and structural damage. This is the #1 grade-line failure mode. The painting contractor must mask the gap, not fill it.

Above-grade foundation coating is exposed to direct sunlight and requires UV-resistant formulation. Below-grade coatings (bituminous, fluid-applied membrane) are NOT UV-stable and will degrade rapidly if exposed above grade. The above-grade cosmetic coating must be a UV-resistant acrylic or cementitious coating (e.g., Drylok-type). This is a material selection constraint, not an estimation factor.

relevant_findings.topic: Coating material categories for above-grade foundation
relevant_findings.finding: Two primary coating categories for above-grade foundation: (1) Cementitious/crystalline coatings (e.g., Drylok, UGL) — fills pores, breathable, matte finish, excellent adhesion to concrete, budget-friendly, easy to apply. (2) 100% Acrylic exterior masonry paint — standard exterior coating, wider color range, better aesthetics, semi-gloss/satin available. Both are appropriate for QT2-QT3 utilitarian foundation work. Elastomeric is overkill for above-grade cosmetic coating.

CMU block foundations require block filler to fill open-cell voids before primer/topcoat application. Same requirement as masonry wall spec — PCA P12 standard (Level 2 Standard Fill). Block filler is a substrate preparation product, not a primer. Applied before primer as a separate task. This is a CONDITIONAL module triggered only by foundation_type = CMU.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives block filler requirement (CMU only), surface prep method (form-release removal for poured, void filling for CMU), and production rate variation. Poured concrete is relatively smooth; CMU is porous with voids.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION. Foundation_type determines prep sequence branching.

condition_drivers.impact: Single NC state for both poured and CMU foundation. Drives full prep sequence: cure verification, moisture testing (MC <= 4%), efflorescence treatment, form-release/laitance removal (poured), block filler (CMU), alkali-resistant primer.
condition_drivers.notes: SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is the only NC-relevant state. Both poured concrete and CMU are cementitious substrates in the same substrate state family.

condition_drivers.impact: QT2: economy — light clean, primer, single finish coat. Budget-appropriate for utilitarian foundation band. QT3: standard — full clean, primer, two finish coats. Higher-end residential where foundation appearance matters. No QT4/QT5 — foundation is utilitarian, not decorative.
condition_drivers.notes: Narrow QT range reflects the utilitarian nature of foundation coating. Foundation band is low-visibility, functional surface.

condition_drivers.impact: Damp-proofing: thin cosmetic/protective coating (<10 mils DFT) for above-grade band in dry conditions. This is the standard NC painting scope. Waterproofing: thicker application (40-60 mils DFT) — EXCLUDED from painting contractor scope. Below-grade waterproofing is specialty trade work.
condition_drivers.notes: Treatment_class is NOT a configuration dimension for this spec — it is a scope delimiter. This spec covers damp_proofing (above-grade cosmetic) only. Waterproofing is out of scope.

condition_drivers.impact: Spray: 500-800 SF/hr (fastest for large continuous runs). Roll: 150-250 SF/hr (standard for smaller foundation bands). Brush: 50-100 SF/hr (detail work, tight areas around pipes/vents). Foundation bands are typically small enough for roll as primary method.
condition_drivers.notes: Unlike masonry wall spec, spray on foundation does NOT mandate backroll — above-grade cosmetic coating on smooth poured concrete does not require forced pore penetration. CMU foundation with spray SHOULD include backroll per masonry doctrine.

quality_differences.description: Economy foundation coating. Light water wash. Alkali-resistant primer (still mandatory on new alkaline concrete). Single finish coat of cementitious coating (Drylok-type) or economy acrylic. No edge precision at grade line. Minimal surface prep beyond basic cleaning.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard NC foundation band. Budget-conscious. Most common tier for foundation work — this is a utilitarian surface.

quality_differences.description: Standard foundation coating. Full water wash with stiff brush. Efflorescence treatment if present. Alkali-resistant primer. Two finish coats with mid-grade acrylic or cementitious coating. Clean transition at grade line and siding interface. Block filler on CMU.
quality_differences.typical_use: Higher-end residential where foundation appearance matters. Visible foundation bands on showcase elevations.

failure_modes.name: Osmotic blistering from coated efflorescence
failure_modes.description: Coating applied over active efflorescence traps salt migration path. Salts continue to move through the concrete and accumulate behind the coating film, creating osmotic pressure that lifts the coating in bubbles. Foundation walls are particularly susceptible due to continuous ground contact and capillary moisture rise.
failure_modes.prevention: Remove all efflorescence before coating. Identify and address moisture source. Verify MC <= 4% at coating surface. Do not coat foundation with active moisture migration.
failure_modes.detection: Bubbling or blistering of paint film with white powder underneath. Recurring blisters after repair.

failure_modes.name: Grade-line transition failure (caulked gap)
failure_modes.description: Caulking the 3/8-inch gap between siding and foundation seals the drainage plane. Moisture trapped behind siding causes rot, mold, and structural damage. This is a CATASTROPHIC failure that damages the building structure, not just the coating. The painting contractor may be pressured to 'seal' this gap but must refuse.
failure_modes.prevention: NEVER caulk the siding-to-foundation gap. Mask the gap during painting. Educate homeowner/GC that the gap is intentional drainage. Z-flashing should be present.
failure_modes.detection: Rotting siding at grade line. Mold odor. Peeling paint on siding above foundation. Soft, spongy sheathing when probed.

failure_modes.name: Adhesion failure from form-release agents
failure_modes.description: Poured concrete retains waxy/oily form-release agents from the casting process. These bond-breakers prevent coating adhesion. Coating applied over form-release agents will peel off in sheets, typically within weeks of application.
failure_modes.prevention: Clean poured concrete foundation with TSP or degreaser. Wire brush or abrade surface to remove laitance and form-release residue. Verify adhesion with tape test on small area before full application.
failure_modes.detection: Coating peels off in sheets or large flakes. Clean concrete surface visible underneath peeled area. Coating slides off when wet.

failure_modes.name: UV degradation of below-grade products used above grade
failure_modes.description: Below-grade waterproofing products (bituminous, asphalt-based) are not UV-stable. When exposed above grade, they degrade rapidly — chalking, cracking, and losing protective properties within months. Painting contractor may encounter foundation where below-grade coating extends above grade line and must NOT topcoat with standard paint over incompatible below-grade product.
failure_modes.prevention: Use only UV-resistant coatings for above-grade foundation. Do not topcoat over bituminous/asphalt below-grade products that extend above grade. Identify coating type before application.
failure_modes.detection: Chalky, brittle, cracking dark coating on foundation above grade. Coating that softens in direct sunlight.

notes_for_materials_manager: New concrete/CMU foundation requires alkali-resistant primer rated to pH 13 (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer). Same primer system as masonry wall spec. Non-negotiable on new alkaline surfaces.

Two coating options: (1) Cementitious/crystalline (Drylok-type) — budget-friendly, excellent adhesion to concrete, breathable, matte finish only. (2) 100% Acrylic exterior masonry paint — wider color range, satin/semi-gloss available, better UV resistance.
CMU foundation auto-adds block filler (PCA P12) — same as masonry wall spec. Separate product from primer.
Coverage rates for above-grade cosmetic coating: acrylic 250-350 SF/gal on poured concrete, 150-200 SF/gal on CMU. Cementitious coating: 100-150 SF/gal (thicker application).
Roller nap: 3/4 inch for smooth poured concrete, 1-1/4 inch for CMU. Nylon/polyester blend for water-based products.
Efflorescence cleaning materials: TSP, stiff bristle brush. Acid cleaning materials are unlikely needed for NC foundation.
Oil-based and alkyd products are PROHIBITED on alkaline concrete/CMU — same blocker rule as masonry spec.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup -> protect -> clean -> prep -> block_fill (CMU only) -> prime -> apply -> cleanup.
This is a SMALL spec — fewer modules and tasks than masonry wall. Foundation band is typically 12-36 inches tall, limited surface area.
Moisture testing (MC <= 4% hard stop) is mandatory before primer application. Stricter than masonry wall spec (12%).
Form-release/laitance removal is a prep task for POURED concrete only. Not applicable to CMU.
Block filler is a conditional module for CMU only — same pattern as masonry wall spec.
Grade-line gap: NEVER caulk. Mask the 3/8-inch gap during painting. Include as a crew briefing/safety note in SOP.
Landscape protection along foundation perimeter — LF-based measurement along foundation wall base.
Spray on CMU foundation should include backroll (per masonry doctrine). Spray on smooth poured concrete does not require backroll.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Production rates: spray 500-800 SF/hr, roll 150-250 SF/hr, brush 50-100 SF/hr. These are per-coat rates.
Block filler application (CMU only): spray 200-350 SF/hr, roll 100-200 SF/hr.
This is typically a SMALL add-on line item. Foundation band area = perimeter LF x band height (12-36 inches). A 200 LF perimeter with 24-inch band = 400 SF total — less than 1 hour spray time.
Coat system: QT2 = primer + 1 finish coat. QT3 = primer + 2 finish coats. Block filler on CMU precedes primer.
Access is almost always ground-level. Foundation band is at grade by definition. No height modifier expected.
Moisture testing: fixed time 0.25-0.5 hr per project (smaller scope than masonry wall).
Efflorescence treatment: 150-300 SF/hr depending on severity.
Environmental conditions EXCLUDED from estimation — per established exterior spec convention.

assumptions.value: Above-grade cosmetic foundation coating only. Visible foundation band 12-36 inches above grade. Below-grade waterproofing excluded.
assumptions.note: This is a painting contractor scope, not a waterproofing contractor scope. Below-grade is specialty trade.

assumptions.value: QT2-QT3 only. No QT4/QT5 for foundation.
assumptions.note: Foundation is utilitarian, not decorative. QT4+ is reserved for visible architectural surfaces.

assumptions.value: Damp-proofing (thin cosmetic coating) only. Waterproofing excluded.
assumptions.note: Treatment_class is a scope delimiter, not a configuration dimension. Waterproofing is specialty trade.

assumptions.value: 4% moisture content hard stop per Foundation Coatings Doctrine.
assumptions.note: Stricter than masonry wall spec (12%) due to continuous ground contact and capillary moisture rise.

assumptions.value: Ground-level access assumed for all foundation work. No height modifier.
assumptions.note: Foundation band is at grade by definition. Even multi-story buildings have ground-level foundations.

assumptions.value: New construction only. Single substrate state (SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY).
assumptions.note: Repaint foundation coating would require a separate spec with different prep considerations.

uncertainties.topic: Block filler coverage rate on CMU foundation
uncertainties.detail: Block filler coverage varies by CMU void density. Foundation CMU may differ from wall CMU in block weight and void pattern. Industry range approximately 75-125 SF/gal.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use 100 SF/gal baseline. Same as masonry wall spec. Flag for field calibration.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine provides spray/roll/brush rates for acrylic masonry coatings but cementitious coatings (Drylok-type) may apply at different rates due to thicker consistency. Likely similar to roll rate for acrylic.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use acrylic roll rate (150-250 SF/hr) as baseline for cementitious coating application. Flag for field calibration.

uncertainties.detail: Exposed foundation band height varies by grade, lot slope, and architectural design. 12-36 inches is typical but could be more on sloped lots. Extreme cases may require ladder access.
uncertainties.recommendation: Default to ground-level access. Note that sloped lots may expose more foundation, increasing SF and potentially requiring ladder on downhill side.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: LF-based — measured along foundation wall base where landscape/mulch/soil is adjacent. Drop cloth at base for roll/brush. Full tarp over plantings for spray.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Adjacent sidewalks/paths at foundation base. Drop cloth runners for roll/brush. Full tarp for spray.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Adjacent patio surfaces. Protection driven by proximity and method.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Foundation is a LOW protection spec. The surface is at grade level with limited overspray risk to adjacent surfaces above. Siding/trim protection above the foundation band is NOT this spec's responsibility — siding/trim protection belongs in their respective specs.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Siding meets foundation at grade line with 3/8-inch gap and Z-flashing. Foundation coating terminates below siding edge. No cut-in required — the gap provides a natural break. NEVER caulk this gap.
Foundation meets grade (soil/mulch/gravel). Coating extends to grade line or slightly below. No edge precision needed — rough termination at soil line is acceptable.
Water table trim (if present) sits at siding-to-foundation transition. Foundation coating terminates below water table. Separate trim spec.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Foundation wall has NO edge work requirements within this spec. The grade-line gap at siding provides a natural termination. Soil/grade provides a rough bottom edge. No precision cut-in needed anywhere. This is the simplest adjacency profile of any exterior spec.

affected_conditions.notes: Foundation work is at grade level. Access modifier is effectively always 1.00. No ladder/scaffold/lift expected for standard foundation band.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are EXCLUDED from estimation per established exterior spec convention. They are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable at bid time.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Less impactful at ground level than elevated work.
Varies by time of day and season. Not predictable at bid time.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Foundation is partially shaded by house overhang. Varies by orientation.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC foundation is always bare concrete or bare CMU. No factory-primed foundation exists. Single substrate state for this NC spec.

output_state.rationale: Foundation coating is typically flat or matte finish (cementitious coatings are inherently matte). Acrylic option may be satin. Output state varies by material/sheen selection.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Siding above foundation may already be painted (top-down exterior sequencing). Light masking at siding edge if finished. Foundation coating is below siding with natural gap separation — low overspray risk.

exterior_substrate_states.description: New, uncoated concrete or CMU foundation wall. Alkaline (pH 12-14 for new concrete). Requires alkali-resistant primer. May have form-release agents (poured) or open voids (CMU).
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Moisture test (MC <= 4% hard stop). Remove form-release agents/laitance on poured concrete. Treat efflorescence if present. Apply block filler on CMU (PCA P12). Clean surface with water/TSP.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Alkali-resistant primer rated to pH 13 (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer). Same as masonry wall spec.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Only NC state for foundation. The 4% MC limit is stricter than masonry wall (12%) due to continuous ground contact.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Not applicable for standard foundation work. Foundation band is at grade level.

scenarios.notes: Standard foundation band 12-36 inches above grade. All work at ground level. No access modifier needed.
EDGE CASE: Sloped lots may expose 4-6 ft of foundation on downhill side, requiring ladder. Rare for NC.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints documented for SOP reference. EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers per established exterior spec convention.

sop_reference_only.note: Foundation concrete may be cooler than air temp due to ground contact/shading.
Stricter than masonry wall. Test with electronic moisture meter at multiple points.

sop_reference_only.rule: 28 days standard, 7 days minimum with alkali-resistant primer
sop_reference_only.note: Same cure requirement as masonry wall — new concrete pH 12-14.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5 degrees F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Foundation surfaces may be cooler than ambient — higher dew point risk.

spray_acrylic.notes: Airless spray on above-grade foundation band. High end for long continuous runs on smooth poured concrete.

roll_acrylic.notes: Roller on foundation. 3/4 inch nap for smooth poured concrete, 1-1/4 inch nap for CMU.

brush.notes: Detail work around pipes, vents, tight areas only.

block_filler_spray.notes: CMU only. Heavy-body material. Same as masonry wall spec.

block_filler_roll.notes: CMU only. 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap roller.

alkali_resistant_primer_roll.notes: Primer on bare concrete/CMU. Roll is the typical primer application method for foundation band.

alkali_resistant_primer_spray.notes: Primer by spray for larger foundation areas.

efflorescence_treatment.notes: Dry brush to TSP wash. Acid wash unlikely on NC foundation.

form_release_removal.notes: Poured concrete only. Wire brush or chemical detergent.

moisture_testing.notes: Smaller scope than masonry wall — fewer test points needed.

water_wash.notes: Low-pressure water wash for new concrete/CMU surface.

key_decisions.topic: Scope limited to above-grade cosmetic coating
key_decisions.decision: This spec covers ONLY the above-grade visible foundation band. Below-grade waterproofing is excluded.
key_decisions.rationale: Painting contractor scope. Below-grade waterproofing (40-60 mils DFT, sheet membrane, bituminous) is specialty trade work. This spec is a small add-on line item for the painting scope.

key_decisions.decision: Only QT2 and QT3. No QT4/QT5.
key_decisions.rationale: Foundation is utilitarian, not decorative. QT4+ quality is not warranted for a surface that is partially below grade, often obscured by landscaping, and has no architectural significance.
Drives block filler requirement (CMU only), surface prep method (form-release removal for poured, void filling for CMU), and roller nap selection.

key_decisions.topic: Treatment_class as scope delimiter, not config dimension
key_decisions.decision: Treatment_class (damp_proofing vs waterproofing) is a SCOPE DELIMITER. This spec is damp_proofing only.
key_decisions.rationale: Waterproofing is out of scope for painting contractors. Including it as a config dimension would create a false impression that the painting contractor can spec waterproofing systems.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Single spec covers prep, prime, and finish.
key_decisions.rationale: Foundation coating is a single-mobilization scope. Same crew primes and paints. Small enough scope that splitting would create unnecessary overhead.

key_decisions.topic: Grade-line gap — hard rule against caulking
key_decisions.decision: NEVER caulk the siding-to-foundation gap. Include as SOP hard stop and crew briefing note.
key_decisions.rationale: Caulking the 3/8-inch drainage gap is the #1 grade-line failure mode per doctrine. Causes catastrophic moisture damage to siding and sheathing.

key_decisions.decision: Moisture content hard stop at 4%, not 12%.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Foundation Coatings Doctrine. Stricter than masonry wall spec due to continuous ground contact and capillary moisture rise through foundation.

key_decisions.decision: Ground-level access assumed. No height modifier by default.
key_decisions.rationale: Foundation band is at grade by definition. Even multi-story buildings have ground-level foundations. Sloped lots are an edge case noted in uncertainties.

key_decisions.topic: Block filler as conditional module for CMU
key_decisions.decision: Block filler is a SEPARATE MODULE triggered only by foundation_type = CMU.
key_decisions.rationale: Same pattern as masonry wall spec. Block filler fills voids (PCA P12), is not a primer. Poured concrete does not require block filler.

key_decisions.decision: Oil-based and alkyd products PROHIBITED. Hard blocker rule.
key_decisions.rationale: Same as masonry wall spec. Saponification on alkaline concrete/CMU is catastrophic and irreversible.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Drives block filler requirement (CMU only), surface prep branching (form-release removal for poured, void filling for CMU), and roller nap selection. Not captured by existing PS keys.
proposed_new_keys.notes: Project-level configuration. Most foundations are single type.

research_corrections.rationale: Poured concrete and CMU are both Portland-cement-based with similar alkalinity and primer requirements.

research_corrections.corrected: Environmental conditions EXCLUDED from estimation per established exterior spec convention.
research_corrections.rationale: Same convention as all exterior specs — unpredictable at bid time, SOP concern only.

research_corrections.corrected: Landscape protection is LF-based (perimeter along foundation base), not SF-based.
research_corrections.rationale: Measured along foundation wall base where landscape meets structure.

research_corrections.corrected: No substrate condition modifier — this is an NC spec. All foundation arrives bare.
research_corrections.rationale: NC spec has single substrate state. Condition modifiers apply to repaint specs with variable existing conditions.
